messages:
Priya (Sales): Hey @channel — FinHealth execs want an EU-only POC. They asked for (1) sub-processor list for EU regions, (2) egress/CIDR ranges they can whitelist, (3) rough monthly egress cost for ~5M tokens. Can ops/solutions/security confirm what we can commit for a 6-week POC?
Carlos (Solutions): We can offer tenant pinning to eu-west-1 for data plane and keep control-plane signaling in eu-west-1. Subproc list: Google Cloud (GCP EU), Cloudflare EU edge, and Datadog EU for monitoring. I'll pull the formal attestation and list of EU subprocessors.
Ryan (NetOps): Quick clarifying Q — do they want private peering or just fixed public egress IPs? If peering, we'll need ASN + preferred IX and an LOA.
Priya (Sales): They prefer peering but said fixed IPs are acceptable for the POC if peering is blocked. Legal needs stable ranges to include in their firewall.
Ryan (NetOps): For Dedicated or a reserved POC we can provide two static NAT egress IPs. For fully hosted transient usage the IPs may rotate.
Priya (Sales): Are those two IPs guaranteed for the POC duration? We need language to put in the SOW.
Ryan (NetOps): Yes — if we reserve capacity and allocate a NAT GW for the tenant, the two /32s are stable for the reservation window.
Anya (Security): Note: telemetry/metrics sent to Datadog may still cross control-plane if the tenant pin isn't set. For an EU-only attestation we need tenant_pin + control-plane in eu-west-1. I can add that to the attestation draft.
Carlos (Solutions): Proposed routing policy snippet for the SOW / ops runbook:
```
routing:
  tenant_pin: eu-only
  data_plane: eu-west-1
  control_plane: eu-west-1
  egress_whitelist: ["203.0.113.10", "203.0.113.11"]
  fallthrough: deny
```
Priya (Sales): presales-bot — can you attach the POC pricing sheet and a rough egress estimate?
presales-bot: <https://redwood.example.com/presales/poc-pricing|POC pricing sheet> — baseline hosted egress estimate: ~$0.25 per million tokens outbound for EU hosted endpoints. For 5M tokens that's ~ $1.25 plus cloud provider network egress. Dedicated reserved pools get custom rates and likely lower per-token network overhead.
Carlos (Solutions): Ops note: BYO-KMS adds ~1 week to onboarding and may require different attestation language. BYO networking / private peering increases handoff time.
Priya (Sales): Customer also asked for a signed sub-processor attestation PDF. Carlos / Anya — can you produce a draft by EOD tomorrow?
Anya (Security): I can draft today; will need Legal to sign-off tomorrow. Tagging legal for visibility. :eyes: 
Ryan (NetOps): If they go private peering via an IX, estimate 3-4 business days for cloud provider handoff + LOA processing. If they only need NAT egress IPs, that is immediate once reservation is provisioned.
Priya (Sales): Got it. Also please confirm whether Cloudflare edge caching will serve any PII — customer asked specifically.
Carlos (Solutions): Cloudflare is used for CDN/edge routing only; we can disable edge caching for the tenant to avoid any cached content leaving the EU. We'll add that to the runbook.
Priya (Sales): Great. I'll update the customer with the two options (reserved NAT IPs vs IX peering) and the rough cost implications.
Deploy bot: New eu-west-1 reserved NAT IPs assigned: 203.0.113.10, 203.0.113.11
Priya (Sales): Received, thanks everyone. I'll send the SOW draft to legal and loop back here after sign-off. :thumbsup:
